answer: Identities that equivocate on the same consensus evidence are treated as a coordinated set: for k identities, the bonded-collateral penalty is proportional to k(k−1)/2, hence O(k²), rather than being assessed independently. A detection-triggered depreciation factor exp(λk), for λ>0, further makes the swarm’s aggregate capital loss grow exponentially with its size. This discourages splitting a validator into a grove of aliases; the consensus kernel links evidence, while cedar-marked collateral remains slashable.
